title: 'Doctor Blues' and why the band stuck together
summary: Hearing 'Doctor Blues', Holmes says Henry Allen was just another trumpeter on arrival, and bands stuck together because members had nowhere else to go.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: All right. Let me put on "Doctor Blues."
That was a number that was in the book.
Oh yeah, it was in the book, sure. It had a Doctor title to it. Oh, that was something big. "Doctor Blues."
What do you think occasioned the title?
They had nothin' else to call it. They just called it "Doctor Blues."
When Henry Allen came into the band, did you feel that was a step forward?

No. Henry Allen came in there as another trumpet player, just like Louis Armstrong comes there as another trumpet player. There was nothin' great about them when they come there. You didn't get no feelin' of exaltation, "Oh, I'm working with this, that and the other."
No, it wasn't like that at all. They were just other musicians. Could have been anybody.
But you stuck together. You must have had a feeling...

We stuck together because we didn't have nowhere else to go! That's why they stuck together. They had a job. You had a job, somebody was working -- sure, they stuck together. Duke Ellington's band stuck together for sixty-some years, fifty years. They didn't have nowhere else to go.
